Status and scope are accurate.

At fixed q differentiate both scalar terminal-zero times and retain rho_mu=-sum_i Delta_i t_(i,mu) delta_(t_i), where Delta_i is the right-minus-left material jump. The lower and upper parameter Wronskians, the event equality U_i^2=mu^2 V_i^2, and the endpoint square identities give J_mu=-sum_i Delta_i t_(i,mu)U_i^2 and partial_mu A_n=[2mu I_V-(q^2-1)J_mu]/q^2.

Piecewise Pohozaev identities with the same jump convention recover the displayed equivalent dilation-remainder form. This is an algebraic cross-check of all event and endpoint signs and does not substitute the independently oriented q-response for J_mu.

At R=1 solve U=sin t and V=q sin(mu t)/mu. Indexed terminal zeros force L_0=n pi and mu_0=(n+1)/n, so partial_mu A_n=L_0/mu_0=n^2 pi/(n+1)>0. Chebyshev factorization and the double-root and shared-root exclusions prove exactly 2n separated simple labelled switching events for every finite q>=1, including the q=1 closure.

For fixed n and 1<=R<=R_* set eta=1/q and Z=V/q. Sturm and fundamental-matrix bounds compactify L and mu and give a uniform nonzero derivative at each high-mode zero. The max switch inequality and the R9 nodal allocation localize each of the n positive-material cells to an O(eta) neighborhood of one simple high zero, yielding ||rho-1||_L1=O(eta), U=sin t+O(eta), and Z=sin(mu t)/mu+O(eta) in C1.

Blow up the two endpoints of every shrinking positive cell around z_k^0=k pi/mu. After division by eta, the full 2n-event system has a diagonal limiting Jacobian with entries -epsilon_(k,+/-)mu Z_0'(z_k^0), all nonzero. Earlier shrinking cells contribute only higher order cross terms. The uniform finite-dimensional C1 implicit-function theorem therefore gives t_(k,+),mu-t_(k,-),mu=O(eta), paired event-value cancellation, J_mu=O(eta), and I_V/q^2=L_0/(2mu_0^2)+O(eta).

For each fixed finite R>1, choose any finite R_*>R and apply the preceding compact-uniform estimates along a root sequence q->infinity. Then mu->(n+1)/n, L->n pi, and partial_mu A_n->n^2 pi/(n+1)>0. This is a fixed-R, fixed-n conditional sequence statement, not a uniform or simultaneous R,q limit.

If fixed-n all-q small-positive-contrast positivity failed, take strict roots R_j->1+ with partial_mu A_n<=0. Sturm comparison sends mu_j,L_j to the uniform values. A bounded-q subsequence converges through the simple one-sided R=1 labelled word, including q_*=1, while an unbounded-q subsequence is covered uniformly by the compact-R pair-collapse lemma. Both alternatives give the same positive limit, contradicting the assumed sign.
